_readme: This is the single source of truth for which text-generation models JUDO tries, and in what order.
core/text_model.py reads this file at call time — edit here, no code change needed.
Each entry is {id, note}: 'id' is the exact API model name, 'note' says why it is in the chain
and at what position. JSON has no comment syntax, so 'note' IS the comment.
gemini list  = tried only when Groq is unavailable/exhausted, or for multimodal (images) and
grounded web search (actions/web_search.py) — Groq has neither capability.
groq list    = tried FIRST for every plain-text call (huge free quota, fastest).
2026-09-17: user asked for 20 models per provider. Checked exhaustively before answering —
all 5 configured Gemini API keys (config/api_keys.json -> gemini_api_keys) were queried via
models.list(), all returned the identical 58-model catalogue (same tier), and the Groq key's
full 13-model catalogue was pulled from GET /v1/models. The real, working, text-generating
count on THIS account is 12 for Gemini and 7 for Groq — see the _excluded_* lists below for
exactly what was tried and why it was left out (nothing was skipped without testing it first).
Padding either list to 20 would mean adding models confirmed to 404/400/429-permanently — that
makes the chain slower (every real call wastes time on a guaranteed failure first), not safer.
Ordering rule for gemini: Gemma models get 14,400 requests/day on this account's free tier —
far more than any Gemini-branded model (Flash Lite: 500/day, plain Flash: 20/day; TPM is 250K
for all of them alike, so RPD headroom is the real differentiator). Gemma sits first, then Lite
models, then plain Flash, then the self-updating aliases last as a safety net.
Re-verify periodically:
Groq:   GET https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models
Gemini: python -c "from google import genai; [print(m.name) for m in genai.Client(api_key=KEY).models.list()]"
A model that starts 404ing has been retired — delete its entry here.

gemini.note: 14,400 req/day on this account — by far the most headroom of anything here. Verified answers correctly. Try first.
Same 14,400 req/day tier as the model above. One test run hit a transient 500 (server-side), a retry succeeded immediately — real, working model.
500 req/day, 0 used on this account as of 2026-09-17 — most headroom of the Gemini-branded models.
500 req/day, ~14/500 used — second most headroom, same Lite tier.
Preview build of the same Lite family — extra Lite-tier fallback before dropping to 20-req/day models.
20 req/day, unused. Plain Flash tier (not Lite) — verified answers correctly.
20 req/day, unused. Occasionally returns a transient 503 (server overload) — chain just moves on.
20 req/day, 19/20 already used on this account — real model, kept as a fallback but tried near-last since it is the one closest to its daily cap.
Google's self-updating 'always current flash' alias. Currently resolves to gemini-3.8-flash. Safety net in case a dated model name above it gets retired.
Self-updating 'always current flash-lite' alias — same safety-net role, for the Lite tier.

groq.note: Best quality of the models this Groq key can reach. Tried first — ~0.5-1s responses.
Smaller/faster sibling of gpt-oss-120b, near-identical behavior. Second try.
Fastest observed of all candidates (~0.4s). Solid quality.
Content-safety-tuned variant of gpt-oss-20b. Answers plain prompts cleanly; kept as a mid-chain fallback.
Small general-purpose model. Reliable last-resort before the agentic ones below.
Groq's lighter agentic/tool-use model. Answers cleanly for plain text.
Groq's full agentic system — works, but tends to add unrequested commentary instead of a bare answer. Last resort.

_excluded_from_gemini: gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite — 404 'no longer available to new users' on every call, confirmed on this key.
gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-flash-lite, gemini-2.0-flash-001 — 404 'no longer available', confirmed on this key.
gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3.1-pro (bare id) — 404 not found, confirmed on this key.

gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools, gemini-pro-latest, gemini-omni-flash-preview, gemini-omni-1.1-flash — these DO exist (listed by models.list()) but every call returned 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; the dashboard shows 0/0 quota for the Pro/Omni tier on this free-tier account, meaning that 429 is permanent, not transient. Re-test if the account is ever upgraded.

'Live API' models (Gemini 3 Flash Live, 3.8 Live, etc. — shown as 'Unlimited' on the dashboard) — bidirectional-streaming only, confirmed HTTP 400 'only supports real-time bidirectional streaming' on a normal generate_content call. main.py's voice session already uses this API surface separately; it cannot serve one-shot text/code prompts.
Image (Nano Banana / *-image*), TTS (*-tts*), video (Veo), music (Lyria), embedding (Gemini Embedding) models — wrong output type for a text/code prompt.
Checked all 5 keys in config/api_keys.json's gemini_api_keys pool on 2026-09-17 — identical 58-model catalogue on every one, so this list is not key-specific.
_excluded_from_groq: meta-llama/llama-prompt-guard-2-22m and -86m — prompt-injection CLASSIFIERS, not chat models: they return a label, not a generated answer.
llama-3.3-70b-versatile — RETIRED by Groq (confirmed 404 on 2026-09-16). Do not re-add without re-verifying it exists again.

This Groq key's full catalogue is exactly 13 models (GET /v1/models, checked 2026-09-17); 6 are the ones above, leaving these 7 as the entire usable set — there is no hidden larger catalogue to expand into.
